title: IUKA ROAD ACCIDENT
full_story:
The Iuka Fire Protection District was called out Saturday Morning to a motorcycle accident on the Iuka Road.

Marion County Sheriff’s Deputies say 43-year-old Steven Morford ran off the Iuka Road north of the Apple Road and south of Iuka for an unknown reason at about 7:10 Saturday morning.  The motorcycle then went through the roadside ditch and went airborne before coming to a stop.

Morford was transferred to an Air Evac helicopter and then to St. Louis University Hospital.

title: PROM
full_story:
The Flora Prom will be held next Saturday, April 25th at the New Beginnings Church.  Prom theme is “Midnight on the River” and the dance will run from 8 until 10:30 pm.

The promenade lineup will start at 6:30 pm on West North Avenue between Galaxie Gaming and Ace Hardware.  Vehicles will take a right on 3rd Street to Thomas Street, turn right and then left into the New Beginnings Church parking lot where students will unload and be announced in front of the main entrance.

Anyone wanting to watch the promenade may bring a lawn chair and watch from the designated viewing area in the parking lot.  Following Promenade, the Senior Court family with tickets may enter at 7 pm.  All other spectators can enter after Promenade.

Coronation will follow and will be held inside the venue.  The king candidates are Benny Allen the son of Ben Allen and Nicole Allen, Dulaney Bullard the son of Kimberly and Bryan Bullard, Kyler Dennis the son of Jeff and Mandy Dennis, Parker Helm the son of Erin and Brandon Helm, and Draven Taylor the son of Carl and Cathy Taylor.  Prom Queen Candidates are Ella Cammon the daughter of Holly Johnson and Ryan Cammon, Elise Duke the daughter of Cole and Kristen Duke, Makenna Hackney the daughter of Joel and Sarah Hackney, Andi Henson the daughter of  Steve and Jenny Henson, and Halle Kitley the daughter of Troy and Amy Kitley.

Kendrick Dugan, son of Kendra Dugan and Reyna Strange, daughter of Dustin and Jordyn Strange will be the crown bearers.

A number of streets around the New Beginnings Church will be closed to traffic to accommodate the promenade.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
With a Blood Emergency in place throughout the Midwest, the American Red Cross is asking area blood donors to get out and give blood at their next earliest opportunity.

In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have two blood drives this week.  The first is tomorrow at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church from Noon to 6 pm.  Then there will be a blood drive on Thursday from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

Those who give blood or platelets at these drives will get a $15 e-gift card to the merchant of their choice.

After these drives the next Blood drives in our area will be on Tuesday, April 21st at the Floyd Henson JR High and then on Tuesday, April 28th at the Flora High School.

title: EFFINGHAM ARREST
full_story:
On Thursday, investigators from the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office and the Effingham Police Department executed a search warrant at 810 South Fourth Street in Effingham.

The search warrant was the result of a joint narcotics investigation conducted by the Effingham Police Department, Effingham County Sheriff’s Office, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.

Execution of the warrant resulted in the seizure of methamphetamine, Fentanyl, and a stolen firearm.  Additionally, investigators located evidence consistent with the use and distribution of narcotics.

Derrick Alan Morrell, 41, of Effingham, was taken into custody for possession of Methamphetamine between 5 and 15 grams, Methamphetamine Delivery between 5 and 15 grams, possession of a Controlled Substance, Fentanyl, Possession of a Stolen Firearm, and possession of a Firearm with a Defaced Serial Number.

The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office were assisted by the Effingham County State’s Attorney’s Office.

Morrell remains in custody at the Effingham County Jail awaiting a pre-trial detention hearing and formal charging.

All suspects should be considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL CONCERT
full_story:

title: FCC LINEMAN RODEO
full_story:
On Saturday the Frontier Community College Lineman Rodeo will take place starting at 9 am.  The event will give an opportunity for the Electrical Distribution Systems (EDS) students to showcase what they have learned through friendly competition.  Judged events include, egg climb, fuse swap, hurt man rescue, speed climb, and underslung-switch open & close.

Attending the event is a great chance for anyone interested in the EDS program to see things firsthand and to ask questions and learn more.  Frontier Community College combines classroom lectures with extensive outdoor training to prepare you for wire maintenance, hurt man rescue, cross arm construction, and more.  Competition times will be displayed on a leaderboard for participants and spectators to track results throughout the event.

The rodeo will take place outside just north of the Workforce Development Center, so, bring your lawn chair.  T shirts and food will be available at the rodeo.

The EDS program is a 1-year certificate program, for more information, call 618-842-3711.  Additional details about Frontier Community College’s Electrical Distribution Systems program can be found at iecc.edu/fcc/eds.

title: NEW TROOPERS
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) welcomed eight new Troopers Friday from Cadet Class 153 at a graduation ceremony at the Illinois State Police Academy in Springfield.  The new Troopers will report to five ISP Troop locations throughout the state on Sunday.

Cadet Class 153 was a 14-week lateral entry academy class.  The eight new Troopers were certified police officers who previously graduated from an accredited law enforcement academy and had at least two years of experience as full-time officers with other law enforcement agencies.  The program consists of physical and classroom instruction, which includes training in Cultural Diversity, Procedural Justice, Domestic Violence, Critical Incident Response, De-escalation Tactics, Firearms, First Responder Certification, Control and Arrest Tactics, Illinois Vehicle Code, Criminal Law, Motor Carrier Safety, Juvenile Law, and more.

In addition to the 14-week academy training, these Troopers are required to participate in an additional 14-weeks of one-on-one mentoring and field training with ISP Field Training Officers in their assigned Troops, expanding their total training to 28 weeks.  Troopers who successfully complete the field training program advance to solo-patrol status.

New Troopers earn approximately $90,000 in compensation upon graduation from the Illinois State Police Academy.  Anyone interested in joining the ranks of Illinois State Police is encouraged to visit the Illinois State Police Merit Board website at www.illinoistrooper.com for application information.
